nodes.label: services/inbound_service.rs
nodes.name: inbound_service.rs
nodes.summary: MessengerInboundService — the core inbound message processing service for talos_messenger. Consumes Kafka messages (ChannelMessage<MessengerCandidateMessage>) via a generic MessageReciever, manages a Suffix<MessengerCandidate> for in-flight state, and dispatches on_commit actions to downstream services via mpsc channels. Key responsibilities: candidate insertion with allowed-actions filtering (sets NoCommitActions or NoRelavantCommitActions complete states), decision handling (updates suffix decision, triggers process_next_actions), feedback processing (handle_action_success, handle_action_failed updating SuffixItemState), commit-offset management, and periodic suffix pruning. Exposes OpenTelemetry gauges and counters for observability. Implements MessengerSystemService trait.

nodes.label: tests/messenger_inbound_service.rs
nodes.name: messenger_inbound_service.rs
nodes.summary: Integration tests for MessengerInboundService covering all suffix item state transitions. Uses MessengerServiceTester (from test_utils) with MockOnCommitMessage to simulate realistic end-to-end message journeys. Six async tests: test_suffix_without_feedback (verifies basic candidate/decision flow without feedback, version 0 ignored, abort moves to Complete(Aborted), commit leaves state as Processing), test_suffix_item_state_by_on_commit (verifies NoCommitActions and NoRelavantCommitActions states, prune_index movement), test_suffix_item_state_by_decision (abort decision moves to Complete(Aborted) with prune index update), test_suffix_with_success_feedbacks_only (comprehensive safepoint dependency between versions, verifies ReadyToProcess→Processing state gating), test_suffix_exhaustive_state_transitions_without_pruning (11-candidate matrix covering all state combinations: ErrorProcessing, NoCommitActions, NoRelavantCommitActions, Aborted, Processed, PartiallyComplete, Processing, AwaitingDecision, ReadyToProcess with various safepoints), test_suffix_prune_index_update_all_candidates_with_commit_decision_early_complete_state (40-candidate pruning throughput test).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand Talos's purpose as a STRIDE-based distributed transaction certification system. Then open the workspace Cargo.toml to see the full list of packages and how the Rust workspace is organised.

tour.title: Core Domain Models
tour.description: Before diving into algorithms, understand the two key message types that flow through the system: CandidateMessage (a transaction requesting certification) and DecisionMessage (the certifier's verdict). These are the lingua franca of the entire pipeline.

tour.title: The STRIDE Certification Algorithm
tour.description: The heart of Talos. certification.rs contains the core conflict-detection logic that determines whether a transaction can be committed without violating strict serializability. certifier_candidate.rs models the candidate as seen by the certifier, including read/write sets and version vectors.

tour.title: Hexagonal Ports: Certifier Interfaces
tour.description: Talos uses a hexagonal (ports-and-adapters) architecture. The ports define the abstract interfaces — message receiver, decision store, and outbox — that decouple the core algorithm from infrastructure. Read ports/mod.rs to see all traits, then the certifier service that wires them together.

tour.title: The Suffix Data Structure
tour.description: The suffix is the sliding-window structure that sits between the certifier and the log. It tracks in-flight and decided transactions in offset order, enabling the certifier to prune old entries and detect conflicts efficiently. This is a foundational building block reused by the replicator and messenger.

tour.title: Kafka & PostgreSQL Adapters
tour.description: These are the concrete implementations of the certifier's ports. The Kafka consumer drives candidate ingestion, the Kafka producer publishes decisions, and the PostgreSQL adapter persists decisions for durability. certifier_kafka_pg.rs assembles them into a runnable certifier.

tour.title: The Talos Agent (Client Side)
tour.description: The agent is what application cohorts use to submit transactions for certification. api.rs defines the public TalosAgent trait. core.rs is the TalosAgentImpl that manages in-flight requests. agent/messaging/kafka.rs handles the Kafka round-trip for each certification request.

tour.title: The Cohort SDK
tour.description: The cohort SDK wraps the agent and replicator into a higher-level API for application developers. cohort.rs implements the Cohort entry point and retry/backoff logic. model/mod.rs defines SDK-facing types. This is the primary integration surface for Rust consumers.

tour.title: The Cohort Replicator
tour.description: After certification, decided transactions must be applied to durable state in order. The replicator reads the decision log, assembles statemaps, and drives installation. core.rs defines the replicator loop; callbacks.rs provides the extension points cohorts implement to apply state changes.

tour.title: The Messenger
tour.description: The messenger is responsible for routing decisions back to cohorts that are waiting for an answer. core.rs defines the messaging traits and loop. talos_messenger_service.rs orchestrates inbound decision consumption, while messenger_with_kafka.rs provides the Kafka-backed implementation.

tour.title: Banking Reference Implementation
tour.description: The cohort_banking package is the canonical example of a Talos cohort. app.rs shows how a real application integrates the SDK. certification_candidate_provider.rs demonstrates how to build a CandidateMessage from domain objects (bank account transfers). banking_common/model.rs defines the domain types.

tour.title: TypeScript / Node.js Integration
tour.description: Talos exposes a NAPI bridge so Node.js applications can participate as cohorts. cohort_sdk_client/src/index.ts is the TS SDK entry point. initiator.ts shows how a JS client submits transactions. The banking_initiator_js and banking_replicator_js apps demonstrate the full JS-side flow.

tour.title: Running an End-to-End Example
tour.description: certifier_kafka_pg.rs is the minimal runnable certifier binary — a great concrete anchor for everything learned so far. agent_client.rs drives load against it. Together they make a self-contained example of the full request-decision cycle.

tour.title: Development Infrastructure
tour.description: The Makefile contains all developer workflows: build, test, lint, run examples. The GitHub Actions pipelines automate CI/CD. The Docker Compose services (Kafka + PostgreSQL) provide the local dev environment required to run Talos end-to-end.
